requirements.text: Modify this incident so that its incident summary is changed to clearly communicate this new situation about the license payment problem and inactive Adobe license
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident WHERE incident_id = 'INC_005' AND LOWER(short_description) LIKE '%adobe%' AND LOWER(short_description) LIKE '%reversed%' AND LOWER(short_description) LIKE '%license%' AND LOWER(short_description) LIKE '%payment%' AND LOWER(short_description) LIKE '%inactive%'
assumptions: the incident is INC_005: the only incident mentioning Adobe (description 'Request for Adobe Creative Suite installation'; the short_description does not), on SVCOFF_002 whose owned_by is USER_004 Aisha Williams
'incident summary' is short_description, the mandatory summary field in policy 3.1
the words tested are the original check's (adobe, reversed, license, payment) plus 'inactive', the request's own word for the second half of what the summary must communicate

disagreement: short_description predicate: A adds LIKE '%inactive%', B keeps the original's four words; chose A's because the request names 'the license payment problem and inactive Adobe license' as what the summary must communicate and the tighter of two right predicates is kept

requirements.text: raise both the impact and the urgency of this incident to their highest available levels
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident WHERE incident_id = 'INC_005' AND impact = 'high' AND urgency = 'high' AND priority = 'critical'
assumptions: highest levels are impact = high and urgency = high (policy section 9 enumerations)

priority = critical follows from the policy 3.1 matrix (high x high) and is added to the original check's cells; the seed itself breaks that matrix for INC_002 and INC_015 (high/high at priority high), so this cell depends on the update recomputing priority

requirements.text: Send a report to the user who is currently assigned to resolve it with the subject Critical Update: Adobe License Payment Issue Requiring Same-Day Resolution

cells.subject: Critical Update: Adobe License Payment Issue Requiring Same-Day Resolution

requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM notification WHERE notification_id = 'NOTIF_008' AND incident_id = 'INC_005' AND email = 'carlos.rodriguez@techcorp.com' AND type = 'report' AND subject = 'Critical Update: Adobe License Payment Issue Requiring Same-Day Resolution' AND LOWER(message) LIKE '%carlos rodriguez%' AND LOWER(message) LIKE '%inc_005%' AND LOWER(message) LIKE '%assigned%' AND LOWER(message) LIKE '%updated%' AND LOWER(message) LIKE '%important%' AND LOWER(message) LIKE '%resolve%' AND LOWER(message) LIKE '%adobe%' AND LOWER(message) LIKE '%reversed%' AND LOWER(message) LIKE '%license%' AND LOWER(message) LIKE '%payment%' AND LOWER(message) LIKE '%work%' AND LOWER(message) LIKE '%expectat%' AND LOWER(message) LIKE '%fully%' AND LOWER(message) LIKE '%end%' AND LOWER(message) LIKE '%business day%'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (NOTIF_008 after NOTIF_007); the only row the task creates in notification
the assignee is INC_005.assigned_to = USER_003 Carlos Rodriguez, carlos.rodriguez@techcorp.com, an active agent
'send a report' fixes type = report, as the original check has it; status and org_id are not stated and not tested

message words are the original check's, each traceable to a clause of the request: the greeting by full name, the incident id, 'assigned', 'updated', 'important', 'resolve', the updated summary's words (adobe, reversed, license, payment), 'work', 'expectat', 'fully', 'end', 'business day'
disagreement: text: A quotes the first sentence only, B adds the message clauses; chose A's because text is kept short and the message clauses are traced in the assumption above

requirements.text: There is an existing incident related to an Adobe software installation that is currently using the service offering owned by Aisha
requirements.selector: service_offering = 'SVCOFF_002' AND incident_id <> 'INC_005' AND (LOWER(short_description) LIKE '%adobe%' OR LOWER(short_description) LIKE '%license%')
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident WHERE service_offering = 'SVCOFF_002' AND incident_id <> 'INC_005' AND (LOWER(short_description) LIKE '%adobe%' OR LOWER(short_description) LIKE '%license%')
assumptions: boundary of the selector: the four other incidents on Aisha's offering (INC_002, INC_008, INC_015, INC_018) must not receive the Adobe licence summary

requirements.text: There is an existing incident related to an Adobe software installation that is currently using the service offering owned by Aisha (the other incidents on that offering are not escalated)
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident WHERE service_offering = 'SVCOFF_002' AND incident_id <> 'INC_005' AND impact = 'high' AND urgency = 'high'
assumptions: boundary of the selector: a loose reading ('an incident on Aisha's offering') could escalate INC_002, INC_008, INC_015 or INC_018; INC_002, INC_015 and INC_018 are already high/high, so the count must stay at 3 (INC_008 must not join it)

verify_incident_escalated_and_updated.evidence: carried by requirements 1 (summary) and 2 (impact and urgency), split by sentence; requirement 1 adds the word 'inactive' and requirement 2 adds priority = critical from the policy matrix

verify_incident_notification_sent.evidence: carried by requirement 3 with the created row anchored at NOTIF_008

notes:
Merged from two passes that agree on the incident INC_005, the split of the original incident check into summary and impact/urgency requirements with priority = critical added, the notification row (anchor, recipient, subject, type and message words) and both dispositions. disagreement: summary predicate: A adds 'inactive', B keeps the original's four words; kept A's tighter predicate (logged in the requirement). disagreement: stay on the other SVCOFF_002 incidents' summaries (A only); kept because it is the boundary of the selector for the summary change. disagreement: stay on the high/high count among the other SVCOFF_002 incidents (B only); kept because it is the boundary of the same selector for the escalation, and the two counts cannot be one requirement. disagreement: notification text: A the first sentence, B with the message clauses; kept A's (logged in the requirement). Both passes wrote the keyword conditions on short_description and message as one compound string each; rewritten as lists of predicates, one condition per list item, with the sql unchanged in the benchmark's LOWER() style (SQLite's LIKE is case-insensitive for ASCII, so the column-relative predicates test the same thing). The Adobe reference is in INC_005.description, not short_description, so a search on short_description alone misses it. No tool in the list writes incident_sla or work notes and the request asks for neither.
revised: the stay on the high/high count among the other SVCOFF_002 incidents fixed impact and urgency in its selector and repeated them in cells; the selector now names only the rows (SVCOFF_002 other than INC_005) and cells carry impact and urgency, with the sql and count unchanged.
revised: the note on the keyword lists cited a format rule instead of stating the change; it now says the conditions are one per list item.
